standard_prerequisites.name: Linear algebra over F2 and conditional expectations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The solutions of a consistent linear system form an affine space, and a nonconstant affine coordinate is uniform under uniformly random free bits. Conditional expectations can be maintained while fixing these bits.
standard_prerequisites.use: Tools for the included zero-set subprocedure; its actual choice of set and guarantee are not assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Incremental Gaussian elimination and constant-size exhaustive search
standard_prerequisites.use: Maintain an affine-system description while adding forced assignments; solve sparse rows with a maintained basis and process finitely many at-most20-vertex cases.

core_obligations: Use the promised LO2-coloring to interpret forced1 variables as forcing the other two vertices of each incident edge to0, until remaining edges have size2 or3 and no coordinate is fixed.
Extract a zero set of at least half the remaining vertices from the affine solution space, deterministically, whose intersection with each3-edge is0 or2 and with each2-edge is1.
Assign these vertices the smallest unused color and remove every touched edge, so its last uncolored vertex later becomes the unique maximum; preserve the LO2 promise on untouched edges.

Show the no-fixed-coordinate condition persists under removal, bound the number of colors with the constant-size termination rule, and amortize the running time over geometrically shrinking vertex sets.

proof_roadmap.step: Uniformity of each free affine coordinate yields a half-size zero set; fix free bits by conditional expectations.
Propagate forced assignments using the original promise and reduce to a2/3-uniform instance.
Iterate half-removal with ordered colors and prove every original edge has a unique maximum.
Use the constant nonzero count per incidence row for the system-solving cost.
Sum the costs across vertex halvings.

difficulty_reason: The linear system admits spurious all-one triples, so solving it is not itself a coloring algorithm. The proof uses its affine freedom in a different way: a large zero set resolves an edge without destroying the promised structure of the remaining instance. Forced-variable propagation, preservation of free coordinates, deterministic half-removal and the ordered coloring invariant together supply a nonroutine promise-preserving approximation mechanism beyond simply applying Gaussian elimination or the probabilistic method.

compared.difference: The public primary only returns a large zero set under a no-fixed-variable promise. The new claim is a complete coloring algorithm for arbitrary promised3-uniform input, with preprocessing, recursive promise preservation, global coloring correctness, logarithmic color count and total time. The old subprocedure is supplied with its entire proof as support, not counted again.

dedup.scope: Same-source counted primary identified. APPROX24/journal versions and other unique-maximum/LO terminology need final semantic comparison; different names or versions are not separate tasks.

editorial_notes: All arithmetic in the counted algorithm is overF2. The separate rational/continuous-randomness algorithm238-329 is not a premise or an additional counted claim.

At197 the count of repetitions is written without integer rounding. The algorithm actually uses at most ceil(log2(n/20)) iterations when n>20, then at most2 colors; this is still below log2(n), and for4<=n<=20 the2-color terminal step also satisfies the theorem. Preserve the author wording and make the rounding interpretation explicit.

The source runs forced-variable elimination to a fixed point. Incremental elimination, rather than restarting a complete system solve after each individual forced assignment, is the standard linear-algebra implementation behind its stated total running-time bound. The source mathematical proof is unchanged.

review_checkpoints: A forced1 in every affine solution must be1 in every promisedLO2 coloring, so its two neighbors in each3-edge are forced0 by the promise; partially fixed edges at the fixed point have exactly one fixed0.

After deleting T and every touched edge, restrictions of all previous affine solutions still satisfy the remaining system. Thus a previously free remaining coordinate cannot become fixed; the innerstep hypothesis persists.
Parity forces every3-edge to have0 or2 zeroes and every2-edge exactly1, so touched edges have exactly one vertex left, eventually receiving a larger color.
Constant-size final brute force uses the existence promise, not an unverified search experiment.
The current source title uses LO colorings and says this is the same notion as unique-maximum hypergraph coloring; final dedup must compare both names.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: The displayed repetition count197 suppresses a ceiling, but its slack at cutoff20 gives the stated log2(n) bound by the explicitly recorded arithmetic. Confirm this interpretation while retaining the source.
Check that standard sparse-row/incremental Gaussian elimination suffices for O(n^3+nm), including forced-variable propagation; do not silently replace the claimed bound by a weaker polynomial.
Judge the whole promise-preserving coloring algorithm after explicit basic linear algebra, not only the previously counted innerstep or the exponential-improvement abstract claim.

The previously counted subroutine and the second rational algorithm are not separately counted.
